concept_html:
A RAG answer can fail in two places: retrieval missed the passage, or the model misused it. Measure retrieval on its own first. It is cheap and exact, and needs no model call.

Build a gold set. Write questions the way users ask them, and record for each one the IDs of the sections that answer it. Take questions from real requests where you can: users phrase things in ways you do not expect. Mark relevance by section, not by chunk, so a new chunk size does not invalidate the labels. Keep the set in version control, and add every question that failed in use.

Two metrics.

  • Recall at k is the share of a question's relevant sections found in the top k. With one relevant section it is 1 or 0, and its mean over questions is the hit rate.
  • Reciprocal rank is 1 divided by the rank of the first relevant result, counting from 1, or 0 when none appears. Its mean over questions is the mean reciprocal rank (MRR). It rewards putting the answer first, not only somewhere in the list.
def recall_at_k(ranked: list[str], relevant: set[str], k: int) -> float:
    return len(set(ranked[:k]) & relevant) / len(relevant)


def reciprocal_rank(ranked: list[str], relevant: set[str]) -> float:
    for rank, item in enumerate(ranked, start=1):
        if item in relevant:
            return 1 / rank
    return 0.0

& intersects two sets. Rank sections, not chunks: when several chunks of one section come back, keep the section at its first position with list(dict.fromkeys(section_ids)), which drops repeats and keeps order.

Compare settings on the same set. Chunk size, k, the keyword ranking and the filters all change retrieval. Run each on the same gold set and keep the best. Report intervals: 45 hits out of 50 has a 95% Wilson interval of 78.6% to 95.7% (lesson B8-L2), so one question more or less proves nothing.

lines: from collections.abc import Callable
def recall_at_k(ranked: list[str], relevant: set[str], k: int) -> float:
"""Share of the relevant IDs found in the first k of a ranking.
Raises:
ValueError: If relevant is empty or k is below 1.
"""
if not relevant:
raise ValueError("relevant is empty: the question has no gold answer")
if k < 1:
raise ValueError(f"k must be at least 1, got {k}")
return len(set(ranked[:k]) & relevant) / len(relevant)
def reciprocal_rank(ranked: list[str], relevant: set[str]) -> float:
"""1 / rank of the first relevant ID, counting from 1, or 0.0 if none."""
for rank, item in enumerate(ranked, start=1):
if item in relevant:
return 1 / rank
return 0.0
def retrieval_scores(
search: Callable[[str], list[str]], gold: list[tuple[str, set[str]]], k: int
) -> dict[str, float]:
"""Mean recall at k and MRR of a section-level search over gold questions.
Args:
search: Returns section IDs for a question, best first, possibly repeated.
gold: (question, relevant section IDs) pairs.
k: Cut-off for recall.
Raises:
ValueError: If gold is empty.
"""
if not gold:
raise ValueError("no gold questions")
recalls, ranks = [], []
for question, relevant in gold:
ranked = list(dict.fromkeys(search(question)))
recalls.append(recall_at_k(ranked, relevant, k))
ranks.append(reciprocal_rank(ranked, relevant))
return {"recall_at_k": sum(recalls) / len(gold), "mrr": sum(ranks) / len(gold)}

def recall_at_k(ranked: list[str], relevant: set[str], k: int) -> float:
    """Share of the relevant IDs found in the first k of a ranking.

    Args:
        ranked: Retrieved IDs, best first.
        relevant: IDs a person marked as answering the question.
        k: Cut-off.

    Returns:
        A value from 0 to 1.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If relevant is empty or k is below 1.
    """
    if not relevant:
        raise ValueError("relevant is empty: the question has no gold answer")
    if k < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"k must be at least 1, got {k}")
    return len(set(ranked[:k]) & relevant) / len(relevant)

title: Evaluate retrieval, recall at k and MRR on a gold set
why_html: A team spent two weeks rewriting its answer prompt because a third of answers were wrong. A retrieval check on 60 gold questions then showed recall at 5 of 0.68: for about a third of the questions, the right section never reached the prompt. No prompt could fix that. Adding a keyword ranking raised recall at 5 to 0.93, and most wrong answers went with it.
